gap: No result ChatGPT got states the PPS ceiling of any "45 W" 10,000 mAh built-in-cable bank against what a Galaxy needs for 45 W: ChargerLAB read 3.6-11 V at 3 A (33 W) on UGREEN's 45 W Nexode PB603, while Samsung's own 45 W adapter lists PPS 5-20 V at 2.25 A.
standout_why: Compared against Talk Android (never mentions PPS; says only that four of its six are "rated at 45W, which Samsung's fastest phones can use"), Pickstead (PPS 3-11 V at 2.72 A, but only for Anker's 30 W A1259), TechRadar (fetch returned navigation only, article body not read) and the cited anker.com A1638 page. The Anker half of the finding (Samsung 45 W and iPhone 17 40 W on cable and port only; 15 W + 7.5 W when both are used) is already on that cited Anker page. The new half is ChargerLAB's 33 W PPS ceiling, and it is for UGREEN's PB603, not the Nexode Pro our partner store sells at $35.99. I could not read the PPS lines for INIU P41L-E2, UGREEN Nexode Pro 10K or Baseus FC11 10K because their product pages returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today. If those three cells are filled from the makers' pages, this would rise to 3.
decides: For Galaxy S22+/S23+/S24+/S25-class owners who want 45 W, Anker Nano A1638 (ours, Amazon link) is the only candidate whose maker states Samsung 45 W on the built-in cable, so it wins that segment on sourced evidence. ChatGPT's INIU pick for a Galaxy Ultra stays unverified, as ChatGPT itself said. For iPhone buyers the angle does not change the pick: ChargerLAB measured 38.17 W into an iPhone 17 Pro Max from a bank whose PPS stops at 33 W, and Anker states 40 W max for the iPhone 17 series. Two price corrections to ChatGPT's cards: Anker A1638 is $45.99 on anker.com today (it showed $59.99) and INIU Pawsible Slim is $26.99 on iniushop.com (it showed $24.99).

findings.label: Samsung and iPhone ceiling, maker's statement
findings.value: "Only the USB-C port / cable supports 45W max output for Samsung and 40W max output for iPhone 17 series"; "Only the USB-C port and cable support Samsung Fast Charging 2.0"
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker US
findings.note: The USB-A port is excluded from both figures (22.5 W max). This page is one of the results ChatGPT cited.

findings.label: Output lines, built-in cable and USB-C port
findings.value: 5 V 3 A / 9 V 3 A / 10 V 2.25 A / 15 V 3 A / 20 V 2.25 A (45 W max); USB-A 22.5 W max
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker US
findings.note: The product page prints no PPS voltage range and no Wh figure.

findings.label: Output when the cable and ports are used together
findings.value: Cable + USB-C port: 22.5 W max (15 W cable, 7.5 W port); cable + USB-C + USB-A: 22.5 W max (7.5 W each)
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker US
findings.note: 45 W applies to one device only; a second device drops the built-in cable to 15 W.

findings.label: Recharge input
findings.value: 30 W max through the cable or the USB-C port (5 V 3 A / 9 V 3 A / 12 V 2.5 A / 15 V 2 A); Anker says to use a 30 W or higher PD adapter
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker US

findings.label: Lightning iPhones
findings.value: iPhone 14 and earlier need a USB-C to Lightning cable or adapter, not included
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker US
findings.note: The page words this two ways: "USB-C to Lightning adapter is required" in one note and "USB-C to Lightning cable" in another. A cable would go in the spare USB-C port, not on the built-in cable.

findings.label: Price, weight, cable
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker US
findings.note: ChatGPT's card showed $59.99. Anker notes the cable length "is estimated and not marked on the product". No sale end date was read.

findings.label: PPS, maker's support page
findings.value: "The USB-C port also supports PPS 2.0, allowing a Samsung s23 utral to be fully charged in approximately 70 minutes"; "Both the USB-C port and the retractable C cable support 45W output"
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker Support
findings.note: No PPS volt/amp range is given. This page calls the cable 70 cm, which matches 2.3 ft.

findings.label: What Samsung requires for 45 W (Super Fast Charging 2.0)
findings.value: "Super Fast Charging (SFC) 2.0 requires a USB Power Delivery (PD) 3.0 compatible device supporting Direct Charging"; Samsung's 45 W adapter outputs PDO 9 V/15 V at 3 A and 20 V at 2.25 A, PPS 5.0-20.0 V at 2.25 A
findings.source_title: 45W Power Adapter (with Cable) EP-T4511 - Samsung Canada
findings.note: Samsung Canada page, not the US one. SFC 2.0 models listed: Galaxy Note 10+, S20 Ultra, S22+/S22 Ultra, S23 and S24 series, S25 models, Tab S7 and later. Samsung recommends its own 5 A cables. Arithmetic: 20 V × 2.25 A = 45 W, so a PPS range that stops at 11 V / 3 A tops out at 33 W.
